blocks.text: Gun powder is a coarse blend of 75% potassium nitrate (KNO₃), 15% wood charcoal, and 10% sulfur. Charcoal carbon is the main fuel, nitrate is the oxidiser and sulfur is the additional fuel that burns the powder faster. The following reaction in burning takes place:

blocks.prompt: a) What is the function of SO₂ and sulfite (SO₃²⁻) salt in preserving the food?
blocks.explanation: They are reducing agents and antimicrobials (they kill microbes): they stop dried fruits, juices and similar foods from browning and changing colour by oxidation, and they stop the growth of bacteria, yeasts and moulds, so the food keeps longer.

blocks.prompt: b) Give the reaction of S with HCl acid and NaOH.
blocks.explanation:
Sulfur does not react with the dilute, non-oxidising acid HCl (12.10). In hot concentrated NaOH sulfur disproportionates (it is oxidised and reduced at the same time), giving sulfide and thiosulfate:
4S + 6NaOH → 2Na₂S + Na₂S₂O₃ + 3H₂O
